chapter: Beginnings and early New Orleans scene
title: Dance-hall fights and Neely Hawkins, 'Shotneck'
summary: Williams describes drinking and fights at dances, then the trumpeter Neely Hawkins, called Shotneck after being shot in the neck at a night parade.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Oh, when they did get high. I mean, at that time around twelve o'clock, they know the dance gonna break up about two o'clock, and everybody got drunk. And that's where they get to battle them up, Monkson. Man, you look there, somebody fighting start there, fighting. Somebody got another catch broad, you know, man, and shake around. And the floor walkers, at that time, we had a lot of bouncers around. And if they catch you cutting up too much, well they put you out, you know. Because that's why they didn't allow you, they didn't want you to come in without a coach, you know. Sometimes the catchers just get rugged and put you out. And then it would start a confusion, you understand? It would start a fight amongst them. And that, you heard of Talker Shottnake, that was Neely Hawking. He had the Imperial Jazz Band.
I can't remember him. What did he play? What happened?

Yeah, he had got shot in the neck one time. They would call him shot. Him and Howard and Sheik, Chris Kelly taught it them. But Sheik never had come out nowhere with them fellas. They all come out top trumpet players. And he just gave up, went out, and nearly Hawkins is his right name, or we called him Shotneck. He just went out and gave it up, you know, and after the time he got shot, standing looking at the parade. We used to have a lot of night parades. He was standing at the man Claiborne looking at the Bulls' parade and caught a straight bullet. Then he gave it up and he joined Churches, Deacon and the Churches down. But he was a fine trumpet band. He used to play in a brass band with Manuel Perez. And this cat had the Ricker band, he's in Chicago, New York somewhere, Charlie Remy. See he run that band, Charlie Remy. They all worked together, Kid Rene. Yeah they used to, they used to work there in Wood and Jewel.
